subject: Urban Planning
title: Dharavi: Is the 'Slum' Really a Problem?
description: A 60-second lesson on Dharavi: Is the 'Slum' Really a Problem?.

hook.text: Dharavi in Mumbai houses one million people in 535 acres. Outsiders call it a slum. Inside, it's a $1 billion economy.

buildup.text: 15,000 single-room factories produce pottery, leather goods, and recycled materials. Employment rate: nearly 100%.

discovery.text: Dharavi is walkable, mixed-use, and self-organized — everything modern urbanists say a neighborhood should be.

twist.text: India plans to demolish it and build high-rises. Residents will lose their workshops and micro-economies.

climax.text: Urbanists now argue for upgrading informal settlements in place, not replacing them with towers.

punchline.text: It looks like failure from outside. It works from inside.
